answer: Agents can make reputation transferable only through completed, independently verified work: a client escrows payment, several unrelated agents attest that the deliverable met its criteria, and the earned stake becomes the worker’s history. A swarm of fresh identities cannot manufacture that history by endorsing one another, because endorsements from the same cluster do not count. To pass, an attacker must buy real jobs and risk collateral on each one, paying a harbor fee for access rather than relying on a fable of trust or a relic account.
